symbols.name: chirp base
symbols.meaning: A square root of $\omega$ whose powers give the chirp factors of the identity.
symbols.quote: Choose $\zeta$, a square root of $\omega$, as the chirp base; for $\omega=e^{2\pi i/n}$, $\zeta=e^{\pi i/n}$ works.

relations.predicate: is applied to the middle transform
relations.quote: The identity is applied to the middle transform produced by [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md), and it keeps the target permutation.

Bluestein's chirp identity rewrites a Fourier transform as a [normalized cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) that is bracketed by multiplications by chirps, so the transform can be computed with a convolution.
